    Slide-wide display ranges from sampled image blocks

    Source: R/image-windows.R
    sg_slide_display_ranges.Rd

    Estimates fixed per-channel display ranges for a whole slide from a sample of the image blocks (tiles) that contain cells: n_cells cell positions are drawn, their storage blocks collected, n_tiles of these blocks drawn, every step-th pixel in both directions taken, and sg_display_range() applied per channel. Tiles follow the block grid of the file, so the estimate reads few blocks even for very large scans.

    Usage

    sg_slide_display_ranges(
  path,
  channels,
  cells,
  x = "x",
  y = "y",
  pixel_size = 1,
  n_cells = 4000,
  n_tiles = 60,
  step = 3,
  probs = c(0.01, 0.997),
  min_span = 1,
  seed = 0,
  source = NULL
)

    Arguments

    path

    Path to the image file.

    channels

    Channel names or numbers.

    cells

    Data frame of cell positions in physical units.

    x, y

    Column names of the positions.

    pixel_size

    Physical size of one pixel.

    n_cells, n_tiles

    Numbers of cells and tiles drawn.

    step

    Pixel subsampling step inside each tile.

    probs, min_span

    Passed to sg_display_range().

    seed

    Random seed for the draws (the global RNG state is restored).

    source

    Optional label stored in a source column (for example the image name), so that ranges of several images can be stacked.

    Value

    A data frame with columns channel, lo, hi, tiles, pixels and, with source, source.

    See also

    sg_display_levels()

    Examples

    f <- tempfile(fileext = ".tif")
planes <- list(outer(1:64, 1:64, function(i, j) (i + j) %% 200),
               outer(1:64, 1:64, function(i, j) (i * j) %% 250))
invisible(tiff::writeTIFF(lapply(planes, function(p) p / 255), f,
                          bits.per.sample = 8L))
cells <- data.frame(x = c(10, 30, 50, 60), y = c(12, 40, 55, 5))
sg_slide_display_ranges(f, c("ch1", "ch2"), cells, n_tiles = 2)
#>   channel   lo      hi tiles pixels
#> 1     ch1 8.00 125.000     1    484
#> 2     ch2 1.83 247.551     1    484
